Press X to Not Die is one of those FMV indie games that fully embraces the idea of “so bad it’s good” and turns it into its entire identity.
The premise is exactly what the title suggests - you are constantly being thrown into ridiculous situations where the game literally screams at you to press a button or die. And then it proceeds to punish you in the most over-the-top, intentionally goofy ways imaginable.

The gameplay is built around quick time events and simple choices, but the real entertainment comes from how absurd everything is. Characters deliver their lines like they’re in a low-budget B-movie, the situations escalate for no reason at all, and even failing events often leads to hilariously exaggerated death scenes. It’s chaotic, dumb, and self-aware in a way that makes it hard not to laugh.

What really sells it is the tone. The game knows exactly what it is and never tries to pretend otherwise. Instead of being polished or serious, it leans into the awkward acting, weird writing, and ridiculous scenarios, which ends up making the whole experience more fun than it has any right to be.

The good:
- Hilariously bad FMV charm
- Extremely over-the-top scenarios
- Simple but entertaining QTE gameplay
- Lots of funny death animations
- Strong “B-movie parody” energy
- Short and easy to finish in one sitting
- Surprisingly memorable moments
- Self-aware humor that actually lands
- Fun to play with friends watching
- Constantly ridiculous situations

The bad:
- Very short experience
- Gameplay is extremely simple
- Repetition if replaying too soon
- Acting is intentionally bad (may not appeal to everyone)
- Limited depth or mechanics
- Some jokes don’t land
- More of an interactive comedy than a game
- Not much replay value outside curiosity

Overall, Press X to Not Die is a chaotic FMV parody that succeeds because it fully commits to its own absurdity. It’s not deep, it’s not polished, but it’s genuinely funny in a “what am I even playing” kind of way, which is exactly the point.
